items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1996-01-10
items.q: I talk with Al Corbetti, who is a very, very good friend

ctx.x: And even in his book, my pictures right there with him. Yeah. And, you know, because I talk with Al Corbetti, who is a very, very good friend, who was partly raised with Louis Armstrong. In fact, Al is one of the gentlemen who is building, putting that structure. I think I, did I show you a copy of that? Yeah, letter. Yeah. That they're doing this. They've done more, in a sense, in New York for Louis Armstrong than we're doing here in New Orleans. Of course, I can understand the reason why. Because New York was…
Jazz Fest, founding of Jazz Festival. You were involved.

items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1995-08-29
items.q: It's just like the program that Al Corbetti sent me when they put this big building up in honor of Louis Armstrong

ctx.x: How'd you get to be Louis' escort?

I don't know, it just, I tell you what happened. By being in radio and working for a newspaper, here I'm a press man. And everybody in the Zulu Club at that time, they knew me. Especially Ernest Wright who thought the world of me. I was a big name person in New Orleans because he was affiliated with a lot of unions and with churches and so forth and so on. So between Ernest Wright and Jim Russell and Jim Poole who was a big wheel in the Zulus at that particular time. God bless him. So that's how I got to become…
Yeah, that was, yeah. That's about all it would have been.
